lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Date separators and dash styles should be standardized throughout.
U.S. English, currency, and measurement conventions are inconsistent.
items.because: The résumé uses a U.S. context but includes forms such as “analysed” and “tonnes.”

items.says: Several bullets are too long and should be kept to approximately one or two lines.
items.because: Several currently wrap to three lines.

items.says: The treatment of small numbers is inconsistent.
items.because: Numbers such as two, three, four, and six should follow one rule.

items.says: Serial commas should be used consistently in lists.
Realized, projected, and annualized results should be clearly distinguished.
The final résumé should fit on one page.
items.because: There is not substantial additional experience shown that would justify more length.

items.says: The LinkedIn URL should be confirmed as active and customized.
The placeholder contact details and URL should be replaced if they were not anonymized only for the review.
The date of birth and nationality should be removed.
items.because: They are not standard on U.S. résumés, provide no hiring value, and can expose the candidate to age- or nationality-related bias.

items.says: The MBA dates and degree status need to be updated to show whether the degree was awarded.
items.because: June 2025 has passed, so the entry currently looks like a projected completion date.

items.says: A relevant concentration, honor, leadership role, or coursework could be added if it strengthens the product-management profile.
The degree naming and punctuation should be consistent with the MBA entry.
The internship should state whether it was full-time if that is not obvious in the recruiting context.
The 35% conversion improvement should say whether it is relative or a percentage-point increase.
The conversion result needs a baseline, final rate, sample size, or measurement period if available.
The claim that the flow was changed “for all merchants” should be verified or narrowed.
items.because: It may conflict with language elsewhere about pilots and opt-in groups.

items.says: The bullet should clarify the candidate’s role in deciding, designing, testing, or shipping the change.
items.because: It currently emphasizes the product change more than the candidate’s contribution.

items.says: The conversion result should be shown as measured rather than inferred.
The dispute self-service feature needs a scale or impact result beyond shipping early.
items.because: The bullet currently reports schedule performance rather than feature impact.

items.says: The bullet should clarify whether the candidate owned the requirements, facilitated agreement, or contributed as part of a team.
The “two weeks ahead of plan” claim needs a meaningful and documented original timeline.
items.because: The schedule result is useful only if the original plan was meaningful and documented.

items.says: “Analysed” should be changed to U.S. English spelling.
items.because: The résumé is written for a U.S. context.

items.says: The 1.1 million dollar amount should be formatted consistently as currency.
The loss estimate should clarify whether it was annualized from six months of data and what population it covered.
The relationship between the analysis and the roadmap decision should be rewritten more clearly.
items.because: The current ending is grammatically awkward and makes the business case sound like an appositive rather than a clear outcome.

items.says: The bullet should clarify whether the candidate personally resolved the 140 tickets, coordinated their resolution, or reports a team result.
items.because: The current wording may overstate individual ownership.

items.says: The starting and ending queue sizes should be added if available.
items.because: “By half” is less informative without scale.

items.says: The ticket type should be specified.
items.because: It is unclear whether they were defects, support requests, or onboarding blockers.

items.says: The bullet should be retained only if operational execution is relevant to the targeted product roles.
The opt-in comparison is not a credible causal evaluation of the redesign.
items.because: Opt-in and non-opt-in users are self-selected and likely systematically different, creating selection bias.

items.says: The bullet describes an evaluation method without giving a result.
items.because: This makes it weaker than the surrounding bullets.

items.says: If retained, this bullet should be placed next to the onboarding outcome bullet.
items.because: Both bullets concern the same initiative.

items.says: This strong onboarding outcome should be moved nearer the top of the Harbor Payments bullets.
items.because: The strongest product outcomes should lead the entry.

items.says: The bullet should clarify the candidate’s specific ownership of the redesign.
The measurement window and whether the median covered the full pilot cohort should be defined.
The 2,300 merchants should be identified as either all new pilot merchants or the total eligible population.
The result should be confirmed as not relying solely on the biased opt-in comparison.
items.because: The preceding comparison has selection bias.

items.says: Any promotions during the four-year Crestline period should be shown separately.
items.because: Visible progression would strengthen the résumé.

items.says: The late-delivery bullet presents a changed calculation as an operational improvement.
items.because: Excluding weather-delayed shipments changes the denominator rather than improving delivery performance and suggests metric manipulation.

items.says: The 30% reduction should say whether it is relative or absolute.
The baseline error rate and measurement period should be added if available.
The bullet should clarify whether both sites achieved the result or whether 30% is an aggregate.
“Prepares” is inconsistent with the past-tense role.
The bullet needs an outcome, scale, or quality improvement.
items.because: It currently reads primarily as a responsibility rather than an accomplishment.

items.says: The scope of the forecast should be specified.
items.because: Relevant scope could include regions, revenue, shipment volume, or business units.

items.says: The bullet should clarify whether the candidate personally prepared the pack or coordinated contributions from others.
S&OP should be defined if the target audience may not know the acronym.
The calculation behind the 1,800-hour annual saving and whether it was projected or realized should be clarified.
The operational or financial consequence of the saved hours should be added if available.
The bullet should clarify whether the rollout covered all intended depots or only an initial phase.
“Present” should be confirmed as still accurate.
items.because: The project may no longer be active after MBA graduation.

items.says: “Student Venture” should more precisely identify the project as a school project, independent venture, nonprofit initiative, or student organization.
items.because: The current label may be too broad.

items.says: The 3,100 students should be identified as registered users, students with access, or active users.
The nine-ton food figure should explain how it was measured or estimated.
“Tonnes” and the measurement units should be standardized for a U.S. audience.
items.because: The target audience may expect U.S. English and either consistent metric or U.S. customary units.

items.says: The bullet should clarify the candidate’s individual product contribution to the launch.
items.because: The current wording attributes the full launch to the candidate without specifying the contribution.

items.says: The bullet should confirm that two dining halls participated throughout the first-year measurement period.
The bullet should clarify whether the interviews directly identified missed pickup windows as the main problem.
The growth in weekly active users should not be attributed to reminders without accounting for other launches, marketing, or seasonal effects.
items.because: The résumé does not establish that reminders caused the increase.

items.says: “The following term” should be replaced with a specific time span.
The wording should avoid repeating the same “Launched” opening used in the preceding bullet.
items.because: The adjacent bullets otherwise feel repetitive.

items.says: The volunteer shift system should be identified as software, a workflow, or a scheduling process.
“Staff cover shifts” should be defined.
items.because: An external recruiter may not understand the term.

items.says: The measurement period for the 95% fill rate should be added.
The reduction from 10 to two cover shifts should be confirmed as sustained.
The hospital network’s name could be disclosed if confidentiality permits.
items.because: Naming the client may add credibility.

items.says: The project heading should clarify the team size and the candidate’s leadership scope.
The working-sessions bullet needs a concrete purpose, deliverable, or result.
items.because: It currently describes a meeting activity rather than an accomplishment.

items.says: The number of clinics or managers involved should be stated.
The candidate’s contribution as team lead should be made more explicit.
The passive construction should be changed to clarify the team’s ownership without overstating personal responsibility.
The bullet needs measurable impact such as reduced intake time, fewer fields, lower abandonment, or staff adoption.
The bullet should clarify whether the changes were piloted, fully implemented, or merely accepted.
The analysis supporting the decision to shorten the form should be explained.
The merchant-onboarding bullet is duplicated from Harbor Payments and placed under the wrong role.
items.because: It is unrelated to a hospital network and looks like a copy-and-paste error that may undermine confidence in the résumé’s accuracy.

items.says: “A/B testing” should be removed or reconsidered unless the candidate has designed, run, or interpreted randomized experiments.
items.because: The opt-in comparison described in the experience section is not an A/B test.

items.says: The product skills should be ordered by relevance to the targeted roles.
Supported capabilities such as product analytics, prioritization, experimentation, stakeholder management, or discovery could be added.
Competent use of SQL, product-design tools, BI tools, or prototyping tools should be included if applicable.
items.because: Their absence may be noticeable for product roles.

items.says: The résumé should demonstrate analytical use of Excel if Excel is meant to be a selling point.
